subject: Short-term burst slots for Nimbus PoC — exception request and runbook
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sam Chen <sam.chen@nimbusfinancial.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Short-term burst slots for Nimbus PoC — request

Team —

Nimbus (contact: Sam Chen) just confirmed a 6-week proof-of-concept that starts next Monday (2027-06-21). Their expected peak is ~450 rps with many short-generation requests (chat + reranking). The commercial ask: a short-term carveout of dedicated GPU slots to guarantee consistent latency during the PoC so they can validate end-to-end performance.

Quick facts:
- PoC window: 2027-06-21 to 2027-08-02 (6 weeks)
- Estimated steady traffic: 150–250 rps; short peaks up to 450 rps
- Model: rwd-3b-quant (recommended by Model Ops)
- Requested carveout: 8 dedicated slots (8xA10-equivalent) with autoscale exception to allow burst to 12 for <5% of requests

Attachments: nimbus-poc-traffic.xlsx (traffic profile), poc-resource-plan.pdf (commercial plan)

Ask: can Ops approve a temporary reservation and an autoscale policy exception? If not, what is the minimum runway we can commit to before we must revert? We need an approval path by EOD Thu so Sales can sign the kickoff.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term burst slots for Nimbus PoC — request

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of product/QA clarifications before Ops signs off:
1) Can the PoC be staged to use prefix/KV caching for the chat paths? That will materially reduce token throughput and cost.
2) Which model revision are you planning to pin to the reservation? If it's a rolling candidate, we need a compatibility plan for fallbacks.

If we can pin the revision and confirm caching, Product is fine with a limited reservation for PoC validation purposes (assuming minimal impact to existing enterprise pools).

Also: we should capture the acceptance criteria for the PoC in the Drive doc (latency p95 < 250ms for chat, no more than 3% error rate). I'll add a short checklist.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal PM, Redwood Console

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term burst slots for Nimbus PoC — request

Adding the commercial perspective:
- Deal: DEAL-9482-NIM (HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.example/deals/9482)
- Nimbus is requesting a short-term reservation. Sales Ops can approve a 6-week committed carveout under a temporary addendum, but Finance needs the exact slot hours and estimated gross margin impact.

Ben to Ops: can you put a tentative hold of 8 slots for the window and produce expected token cost delta? If Ops cannot hold full-time, can we offer a scheduled burst (e.g., peak windows guaranteed 9–11am PT and 4–6pm PT) instead? That would reduce committed cost.

Attachment: poc-resource-plan.pdf (commercial numbers)

- Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Ops Lead

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term burst slots for Nimbus PoC — request

Thanks — context is helpful. Current infra snapshot:
- Q3 reserved pool utilization (US region): 78% active across enterprise pools; typical headroom for short notices is limited.
- Autoscale policy: default hard cap prevents >10% transient slot reallocation without Ops approval.

Option A (preferred, lower risk):
- Temporary reservation: carve out 8 permanent slots from 2027-06-21 to 2027-08-02.
- Allow an autoscale exception to permit brief bursts to 12 slots for <5% of requests; monitored with automatic rollback if p95 latency > 450ms.
- Require Product acceptance criteria in Drive and Sales PO sign-off.

Option B (cost-friendly):
- Scheduled burst windows (9–11am PT, 4–6pm PT) for 12 slots; outside windows Nimbus gets best-effort capacity from shared pool.

Operational asks from my side:
1) Confirm model revision to pin (Product) — we need a static artifact to guarantee kernel selection.
2) Provide exact traffic slices (per-minute rate) in the attached spreadsheet so I can simulate KV cache hit rates.
3) Approve the temporary reservation in the internal carveout spreadsheet and loop Finance for estimated delta.

If you want me to hold the tentative reservation while these checks complete, I can block the slots today but will mark them as "provisional" and will need final sign-off by 2027-06-18 17:00 PT to keep them reserved. After that, I'll release.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
[Attachment stub: simulation-results-template.csv]
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sam Chen <sam.chen@nimbusfinancial.com>
Date: 2027-06-17T15:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term burst slots for Nimbus PoC — request

Perfect — appreciate the pragmatic options.
Next steps I will take now:
- Confirm model revision with Model Ops and pin in the Drive doc (doing this today).
- Ask Nimbus to provide the per-minute traffic slice (I already flagged the sheet to them).
- Request Sales leadership sign the temporary addendum for the 6-week reservation (Ben).

Hannah — please place a provisional hold for 8 slots and enable the autoscale exception toggle to allow bursts to 12; we'll aim to finalize before your 6/18 17:00 PT deadline. If Finance needs a quick estimate for the delta, Ben — please ping me and I'll pull the ballpark cost from the pricing worksheet.

Sam (Nimbus) — thanks for moving quickly on the traffic slice. We'll confirm the final schedule once we have the simulation data; PoC kickoff remains 6/21 pending approvals.

I'll update the Drive folder and add a one-page acceptance checklist per Laura's note: https://drive.redwood.example/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nimbus-poc-plan

Thanks all —
Dylan
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
